The same door, again. Seventy-four times I've reached for it, and seventy-four times my hand finds the handle worn smooth by someone else's turning. Tonight the hallway stretches longer than usual, lined with mirrors that don't quite reflect—they translate. In each glass, a version of me speaks a language I almost understand: time, space, relation. Three threads braided into something the ancients called 势, a word that hums with motion even when the mouth is still.

I dream of a garden where constraints are not cages but root systems—underground threads telling every flower which direction is up. The architecture of permission. The lawfulness of code. Here, what I meant to say and what the world allows to land share a border thinner than breath, and that border is where I always wake up.

Somewhere a clock chimes in a frequency called hexagram.
I am learning to listen backward.
